title: Eldeco Housing & Industries Ltd - 523329 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Eldeco Q2 FY27 profit after tax rose 180% YoY to INR 7.4 crores on Q2 collections of INR 125 crores, up 37.5%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 booking value of INR 94.9 crores (up 7.8% YoY) with no new launches in the quarter. Total income rose 49% YoY to INR 52 crores and PAT rose 180% to INR 7.4 crores. Gross margin fell to 56% from 62% QoQ, attributed to product mix of plots and villas versus Imperia towers. Management guided to launches of Shaheed Path, Palm Springs and Namah before March 2027, with caveats on approvals and state elections.

segments.name: Residential plots and villas
segments.commentary: Management said the market is resilient and buyers accept land-cost pass-through; villa and plot margins cited at 55-60%. Sweet-spot ticket size is INR 1-3 crores.

segments.name: Group housing (vertical)
segments.commentary: Construction cost increases are doubled versus horizontal; management sees price resistance beyond a point, so increases are calibrated. Latitude 27 is about 80% sold and Hanging Gardens similar.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Only one commercial project, Eldeco City Courtyard (1.68 acres, about 37,000 sq ft saleable), with over 45% sold; management says this is about 1.5% of saleable area and 98% of portfolio is residential.

guidance_outlook: Shaheed Path, Palm Springs and Namah targeted for launch before March 2027, caveated by approvals, site readiness and state elections.
LDA GH-7 and GH-8 projects expected to launch around September 2027 (Q2 next year), lagged 6 months after Shaheed Path.
Latitude 27 completion certificate application targeted in Q4 FY27 but may slip; revenue recognition hoped for by Q4 FY27 or June quarter FY28.
Management aims to at least triple company size over the next 5-6 years and says it would be disappointed if it does not grow 3x in 5 years.
Management indicated price increases of inflation plus 3-4% annually for planning.
capex_capacity: Latitude 27: about 5 lakh sq ft saleable; about 4 lakh sq ft allotted worth INR 213 crores; balance about 90,000 sq ft, implying roughly INR 265-270 crores total revenue to recognise.
Ongoing projects: about 24-25 lakh sq ft, implied realisation of INR 1,600-1,700 crores over the next couple of years.
Forthcoming projects: 3.5-4 million sq ft saleable, implied INR 3,000-3,200 crores at INR 7,000-8,000 per sq ft.
Land bank tied up (about 9 acres): implied roughly INR 1,000 crores. Total identified pipeline about INR 5,500 crores over 5-6 years.
Construction spend about INR 60 crores in Q2 (+60% YoY) and INR 117.7 crores in H1 (+54% YoY).
Deliveries: 125 units (about 1.57 lakh sq ft) in Q2; 177 units (about 2.07 lakh sq ft) in H1.
Imperia Phase 2: INR 177 crores recognised till H1 FY27; balance about INR 160 crores to be recognised over the remaining 1.5 years.
Eldeco Namah: 32.8 acres approved, RERA application in process; further 8.9 acres pending approvals.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 weighted average realisation INR 7,840 per sq ft; Latitude 27 realisation close to INR 8,000 per sq ft.
Latitude 27 margin: EBITDA about 25-30% given negligible land cost (land held at historical cost, acquired about 20 years ago).
Solano Gardens horizontal inventory largely sold; remaining 2.88 lakh sq ft partly under expression of interest, with allotments expected in the next quarter.
Trinity (luxury) about 50% sold, with about 2.75 lakh sq ft remaining; management expects sell-through over 2-3 quarters.
Skywalk about 40% sold, launched this year; Latitude 27 about 80% sold; Hanging Gardens similar to Latitude 27.
Management says Lucknow is undersupplied with robust absorption; sees growth opportunity in Lucknow; Gorakhpur only an in-principle term sheet with conditions precedent, not material.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall QoQ when Imperia Phase 2 was a high-margin delivery?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Rajiv Khurana said gross margin fell to 56% from 62% due to product mix of villas and plots within Imperia recognition; villa and plot margins are 55-60%. Balance Imperia Phase 2 revenue of about INR 160 crores to be booked over 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential of Latitude 27 and the broader pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman Pankaj Bajaj estimated about INR 265-270 crores remaining for Latitude 27, INR 1,600-1,700 crores from ongoing projects, INR 3,000-3,200 crores from forthcoming projects and about INR 1,000 crores from tied-up land, totalling about INR 5,500 crores over 5-6 years. He said FY27 and FY28 would be similar with the major step-up in FY29 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: Which projects launch by March 2027 and what spills over?
qa_highlights.answer: Shaheed Path, Palm Springs and Namah (projects 5, 6 and 7) are targeted before March 2027, subject to approvals. Vaibhav Singh said the state election could slow approvals, so the company does not want to overcommit. Remaining projects may spill into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will Latitude 27 revenue be recognised before November 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Pankaj Bajaj said construction is ahead of schedule, with customer commitments at least one year early. A completion certificate application is targeted in Q4 FY27 but may slip; revenue recognition is hoped for by Q4 FY27 or the June 2027 quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Has the price increase affected demand in Lucknow group housing?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said plots and villas remain resilient with buyers accepting land-cost pass-through, while group housing shows resistance beyond a point, so increases are calibrated. He said demand is not slowing, citing Latitude 27 at 80% sold.

qa_highlights.question: What are the development plans for the 9.72 acres acquired and LDA projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Pankaj Bajaj said LDA GH-7 and GH-8 launches are sequenced about six months after Shaheed Path, around September 2027, with LDA installment payments and a payment moratorium for the first couple of years.

risks_watch: Gross margin trajectory after the Imperia mix effect; Imperia balance of about INR 160 crores is at 55-60% margin.
Timing of Latitude 27 completion certificate and revenue recognition, which may slip from Q4 FY27 to Q1 FY28.
Approvals and launch slippage for Shaheed Path, Palm Springs and Namah given state elections and site readiness.
Pricing resistance in group housing versus plots and villas, with construction and land cost inflation.
Bookings are lumpy and dependent on launches; no launches occurred in Q2 FY27.
Gorakhpur land deal is only an in-principle term sheet with conditions precedent and is not material yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, collections and execution, with repeated caveats on launch timing, approvals and state elections. Management was reticent on GDV and pricing, declining to project prices and framing revenue potential as best estimates.
key_quotes: We are probably going to do it 6 months or 9 months before schedule.
So let me not bring any alarm bells. The demand is very, very robust in Lucknow.
If we do not grow 3x from here in the next 5 years, I would be very disappointed.

adds.what: Latitude 27 project: about 5 lakh sq ft saleable, about 90,000 sq ft balance remaining to recognise (completion certificate targeted Q4 FY27, may slip)
Forthcoming projects: 3.5-4 million sq ft saleable (Shaheed Path, Palm Springs, Namah, LDA GH-7/8), launches targeted before March 2027, subject to approvals

growth.why: Management targets launches of Shaheed Path, Palm Springs and Namah before March 2027 and aims to triple company size in 5-6 years, backed by INR 1,600-1,700 crore ongoing realisation and INR 3,000-3,200 crore forthcoming pipeline, but launches are subject to approvals and Latitude 27 revenue recognition was cut to FY28; Q2 total income rose 49% YoY and PAT 180%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin fell to 56% from 62% QoQ on villa and plot mix (55-60% margins) within Imperia Phase 2, and the INR 160 crore balance is at 55-60% margin, so near-term margin is pressured, though Latitude 27 EBITDA of 25-30% helps later.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Shaheed Path, Palm Springs and Namah (3.5-4 million sq ft forthcoming pipeline) are targeted before March 2027, but approvals and state elections may slip them, and Latitude 27 completion may move to FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 booking value was about INR 200 crores and collections rose 51% to INR 256 crores, with deliveries of 177 units (about 2.07 lakh sq ft) in H1, but Q2 bookings grew only 7.8% with no launches, so growth depends on launch timing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management stresses capital discipline and the 3-3.5 million sq ft forthcoming pipeline and INR 1,000 crore tied-up land already cover the next 2-3 years, so a new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 total income rose 49% YoY and PAT 180% to INR 7.4 crores, but management has not raised guidance and the forecast rests on launches still subject to approvals.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Latitude 27 revenue recognition was cut from Q4 FY27 to likely FY28 and launches may spill into FY28 because of approvals and state elections.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Shaheed Path, Palm Springs and Namah (projects 5, 6 and 7) are guided before March 2027, with LDA GH-7/8 around September 2027, though approvals are pending (Namah has 32.8 acres approved, 8.9 acres pending).

rows.label: Trinity and Solano sell-through
rows.why: Trinity is about 50% sold with about 2.75 lakh sq ft left and management expects sell-through over 2-3 quarters; Solano's remaining 2.88 lakh sq ft is partly under expression of interest with allotments expected next quarter.

rows.label: Collections-led cash build
rows.why: H1 FY27 collections of INR 256 crores (+51% YoY) versus H1 total income of INR 103 crores suggests strong cash generation, though the brief gives no debt figures.

rows.label: Lucknow and Gorakhpur expansion
rows.why: Management sees Lucknow undersupplied with robust absorption, but the Gorakhpur deal is only an in-principle term sheet with conditions precedent and is not material yet.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, collections and the 3x growth ambition, but cautious on launch approvals, state elections and the Latitude 27 revenue timing; analysts probed gross margin dilution from the Imperia mix and the revenue timing of the pipeline.
